title: The Resilience Technical Committee's eligibility bar demands dual-domain expertise plus total exclusivity, and currently yields one member
content:
A.2.9.1.1.1.2.2.1 through .2.2.5 stack five requirements on Resilience Technical Committee members: current or prior standing in the legal industry or at "a world-leading insurance broker, insurance company, or risk management firm"; "at least three (3) years of experience managing self-insurance instruments or ... legal or regulatory risk analysis"; "a law, management, risk, or insurance professional degree"; "at least three (3) years of experience in the cryptocurrency, DeFi, Web3, or emerging technology sectors"; and no involvement "in any business activity outside Sky or in any role within Sky that could result in a conflict of interest, either directly or indirectly."

Each requirement is individually justifiable — the Committee assesses claims at "sole and absolute discretion," so competence and independence both matter. But the conjunction is severe: senior insurance and legal professionals with three years of crypto exposure are rare, and the conflicts clause excludes precisely those who maintain the outside practice that produced the expertise.

The consequence is visible in the Active Data: A.2.9.1.1.1.2.3.0.6.1 lists a single active member, Gallagher. A committee of one, selected and paid by the Core Facilitator (A.2.9.1.1.1.2.1), holds absolute discretion over the first gate of every claim.

That is a concentration risk the eligibility bar created rather than prevented. Requirements written to guarantee independent expert judgment have produced a body too small to deliberate, and one whose unavailability would stall the claim process entirely.
description: Members need legal/insurance industry standing, a professional degree, 3+ years in self-insurance or risk, 3+ years in crypto, and no outside business activity at all
